identity.title: Radial pulse irregularly irregular on palpation (>=20-30 s)

technique.how: Palpate the radial pulse with two fingers for at least 20-30 s (longer if any irregularity), noting rhythm and rate. An irregularly irregular rhythm with no repeating pattern and variable beat volume is positive; occasional dropped or early beats with an otherwise regular rhythm are not.
technique.prerequisites: Patient at rest; count for 30-60 s if rate is needed, since pulse deficit in AF makes short counts inaccurate.
technique.contraindications: None. Weak or thready pulse (shock, arterial disease) reduces reliability; use apical auscultation instead.

interpretation.positive_finding: An irregularly irregular pulse raises the probability of atrial fibrillation (pooled LR+ 3.4-5.2) but is not diagnostic; frequent ectopy, sinus arrhythmia and flutter with variable block mimic it, so a 12-lead ECG is required.
interpretation.negative_finding: A regular pulse makes AF unlikely (pooled sensitivity 92-94%, LR- 0.10), which is the finding's main value; it does not exclude paroxysmal AF outside the examination.
interpretation.pitfalls: Specificity is only 72-82%, so roughly a quarter of positive pulses in screening are not AF. Atrial flutter with fixed block feels regular, and AF with slow ventricular response can be hard to appreciate.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: obtain 12-lead ECG now (rate control/anticoagulation decisions follow ECG); negative: AF at this moment unlikely, consider ambulatory monitoring if paroxysmal AF suspected.

estimates.population: 3 studies, 2385 patients, predominantly elderly/primary-care screening populations
estimates.quote: Pooled sensitivity was 94% (95% confidence interval [CI], 84%-97%) and pooled specificity was 72% (95% CI, 69%-75%).
estimates.location: Abstract, Results (LRs: 'The pooled positive likelihood ratio was 3.39, while the pooled negative likelihood ratio was 0.10', same paragraph)

estimates.target_condition: Atrial fibrillation (pulse irregularity detected by manual pulse palpation)
estimates.population: Adults in AF screening studies; 6 pulse-palpation interventions within 21 studies (15,129 pulse assessments overall)
estimates.quote: pulse palpation (six interventions) were 0.92 (95% CI 0.85-0.96) and 0.82 (95% CI 0.76-0.88), respectively (PLR 5.2 (95% CI 3.8-7.2), NLR 0.1 (95% CI 0.05-0.18))

sources.citation: Cooke G, Doust J, Sanders S. Is pulse palpation helpful in detecting atrial fibrillation? A systematic review. J Fam Pract. 2006;55(2):130-134.

Taggar JS, Coleman T, Lewis S, Heneghan C, Jones M. Accuracy of methods for detecting an irregular pulse and suspected atrial fibrillation: A systematic review and meta-analysis. Eur J Prev Cardiol. 2016;23(12):1330-1338.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not rely on pulse palpation instead of an ECG when AF would change management (anticoagulation, rate control, syncope/stroke workup); do not use a weak or thready pulse in shock to judge rhythm.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Irregularly irregular pulse with a rapid rate and hypotension, chest pain, or acute focal deficit requires immediate ECG and monitored care.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Palpation accuracy varies with examiner experience and palpation duration; screening studies mostly used nurses/GPs, and shorter palpation lowers sensitivity for paroxysmal or slow AF.

extraction_notes: Both pooled estimates come from abstracts (no PMC full text). Cooke 2006 pools 3 screening studies (n=2385) and reports LRs without CIs; Taggar 2016 pools 6 pulse-palpation interventions with bivariate CIs and is the larger, more recent analysis. Both are screening/primary-care populations against 12-lead ECG, so performance in symptomatic ED patients (palpitations, syncope) may differ; no ED-specific cohort was found within budget. The 20-30 s palpation duration in the title is convention and not separately quantified.
